newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants to try Zaire envoy over car accident.
newsitem.headline: France wants to try Zaire envoy over car accident.

text.p: France has formally asked Zaire to lift the diplomatic immunity of its ambassador to Paris so that he can be tried for running over two French boys with his car, killing them.

Diplomatic sources said that France's envoy in Kinshasa had delivered a written request on Monday from Foreign Minister Herve de Charette to the Zairean government after an initial request went unanswered.
The letter was released to reporters after de Charette met the mothers of the dead boys for over an hour at the Foreign Ministry.
"It is nearly Christmas. French families will be with their children. But for the families of these boys, it will be a day of sadness and sorrow," De Charette told reporters after the meeting.
"Diplomatic immunity exists so that diplomats can fulfil their mission, not so they can escape the law," he added.

A car driven by envoy Ramazani Baya hit the two boys on a pedestrian crossing in the Riviera resort of Menton. Raphael Lenoir, 13, was killed instantly and Ronald Lehartel, 12, died a week later in hospital.

The mothers are campaigning to bring Baya to trial for the accident, which occurred exactly one month ago. They urged the French public to write to them at the Menton town hall so the letters could be forwarded to Zaire in the form of a petition demanding that Baya's immunity be lifted.

"Give our children a Christmas present. They won't have Christmas any more," Lehartel's mother, who gave her name only as Mrs Belleau, said before television cameras as Lenoir's mother, Germaine Lenoir, sobbed on a relative's shoulder.
French police have said that Baya, on his way to visit Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko at his nearby villa, was driving at 100 kph (60 mph) in a 45-kph (30-mph) zone.

"You certainly understand why it would be unacceptable for the families, which have been seriously affected, if justice were not allowed to be done in such a tragic case, whatever the nationality of the person who caused the accident," de Charette said in the letter to Zairean Foreign Minister Kititwa Tumansi.
De Charette wrote that Baya was also deeply affected by the accident and had reacted with dignity by offering to renounce his immunity.
Under the Vienna Convention, however, a diplomat may not renounce his immunity. Only the state which appointed him can lift it, de Charette said.
